speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress. To help me understand your condition, please tell me exactly when the difficulty breathing started and if you noticed any coughing or sneezing before this?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN). The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant developing respiratory distress within 2 hours of birth, with an uneventful prenatal history, is classic for retained fetal lung fluid. I recommend a Chest_X-Ray to confirm hyperinflation and fluid retention before discharge.
